name: Bina – No Code Form Builder for Contact Form 7
author: webeantech

sections.description:
Bina turns Contact Form 7 into a visual form builder. You do not switch plugins, nothing is migrated, and there is nothing to be locked into.

Import an existing CF7 form with one click, edit it by dragging fields around, and push it back live when you are happy. You never touch shortcode syntax or markup.

One thing worth knowing up front: pushing a form live regenerates its markup. Your fields, names, options and mail settings are kept, but any custom HTML around them is rebuilt in Bina’s layout. That is exactly why an import arrives as a draft, why there is a preview, and why every push can be rolled back for 24 hours.

Contact Form 7 does not save submissions on its own. Bina saves every entry to your own WordPress database, where you can search them, mark them read, and export the lot to CSV.

You can also style Contact Form 7 without CSS. Pick colors, spacing and fonts for one form at a time and watch the preview change as you go.

If you would rather describe a form than draw it, Bina can draft one. Write “job application with a CV upload” and read what comes back before anything is created. That part runs on your own API key from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, and stays switched off until you add one.

Your forms stay Contact Form 7 forms. Bina writes ordinary CF7 markup, so your mail settings, your integrations and your CF7 add-ons carry on working exactly as before.

Why use a visual builder instead of Contact Form 7 shortcodes

CF7 still handles submission, validation and mail, so there is nothing to migrate and nothing to be locked into. Deactivate Bina whenever you like and your forms keep working as normal Contact Form 7 forms.

Imports arrive as a draft. Your live form changes only when you push it, you get a preview first, and any push can be rolled back with one click for the next 24 hours.

Every submission is stored in your own database rather than only emailed out.

Bina sends nothing off your site unless you switch it on: anonymous usage statistics, or the AI generator with your own provider key. Your form entries and your visitors’ personal data stay on your server in every case.

The front end weighs under 15KB, and its styling applies only to the forms Bina manages.

Features

  • One-click import of any existing Contact Form 7 form. Nothing changes until you push.
  • A drag-and-drop builder with responsive multi-column layouts you can resize, which is the two-column Contact Form 7 layout that normally needs hand-written CSS, plus a hover toolbar for move, duplicate and delete, keyboard shortcuts, and undo/redo.
  • Every submission saved to your own WordPress database, with read and unread states, search, and CSV export in one click.
  • The CF7 field types you actually use: text, email, textarea, dropdown, checkboxes, radio, file upload, date, number, URL, tel, hidden, acceptance, quiz. Tags from CF7 add-ons are preserved and keep working.
  • Every CF7 option too. Min and max, placeholder, autocomplete, readonly, akismet, custom classes and ids all round-trip without loss.
  • Edits saved as a draft, with conflict detection if somebody edited the form in the CF7 admin meanwhile, and a 24-hour rollback after every push.
  • Autosave, so your work survives a crash or an accidentally closed tab.
  • A front-end preview that renders the form on the front end, with your theme’s styles.
  • Lightweight, low-specificity styling applied only to Bina-managed forms. Your other CF7 forms are never restyled, and one filter turns it off entirely.
  • Style Contact Form 7 without writing CSS: colors, spacing, fonts, borders and field height, with Normal, Hover and Focus states and a live preview. The styling is scoped to one form at a time and the layout stays standard CF7.
  • Optional AI generation: write “job application with CV upload”, read what comes back, ask for changes, then create the form. It uses your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, and does nothing at all until you add one.
  • A code view, for when you want to read the CF7 markup Bina wrote.

Who this Contact Form 7 builder is for

Agencies and freelancers looking after Contact Form 7 on a lot of client sites, who would rather not hand-edit shortcodes any more.

Site owners who trust CF7 but want a proper editor and somewhere to read what people sent.

Anyone who has lost an enquiry because the form only ever sent an email.

Getting started

  1. Install Contact Form 7 (free) and activate it. Bina builds on top of it.
  2. Install Bina from the Plugins screen under Add New, searching for “Bina”, or upload the plugin ZIP. Activate it.
  3. Open the new Bina menu, pick any Contact Form 7 form, and click Migrate to Bina. Or start a new form from scratch.
  4. Edit it, preview it, then press Push to Live. Your live form does not change until you push, and you can roll any push back within 24 hours.

Requirements

  • Contact Form 7 (free), installed and active.
sections.faq:
How do I edit Contact Form 7 forms without shortcodes?

Install Bina alongside Contact Form 7, open the Bina menu, and import any form you already have with one click. From there you drag fields into place instead of typing tags like [text* your-name]. The shortcode is still written, correctly, every time you push the form live. You just never have to write it yourself.

How do I save Contact Form 7 entries to a database?

Contact Form 7 emails a submission and then forgets it. Bina writes every submission to a table in your own WordPress database as well, so an enquiry that never arrives by email is still there. Entries have read and unread states, search across everything a visitor typed, and one-click CSV export. Nothing is sent to us or to anyone else.

How do I style Contact Form 7 without CSS?

Open a form in Bina and use the Appearance panel. Colors, spacing, fonts, borders, corner radius and field height are all controls, with Normal, Hover and Focus states for fields, Normal and Hover for the submit button, and a live preview beside them. The styling is scoped to that one form, so your other forms are untouched, and the markup stays standard Contact Form 7.

How do I create a two-column Contact Form 7 layout without CSS?

Drag a row onto the canvas, drop fields into it, and pull the divider to set the widths. Contact Form 7 has no layout syntax of its own, so this is normally hand-written CSS. Bina writes the markup and the styles for you, and the form is still a plain Contact Form 7 form.

Will importing my Contact Form 7 form break the live form?

Importing does not touch your live form. It creates a draft. The live form changes when you press Push to Live, and that is when Bina regenerates the markup: fields and options are kept, custom HTML wrappers are rebuilt into Bina’s layout. Preview first, and use the 24-hour rollback if anything looks wrong.

Does Bina replace Contact Form 7?

No. Bina is a builder that sits on top of it. CF7 keeps handling submission, validation and mail. Deactivate Bina and your forms carry on as normal CF7 forms.

Is Bina free?

Yes. This version is completely free and includes the whole visual builder, one-click Contact Form 7 import, entry storage with CSV export, the front-end preview and the styling.

Can I generate a Contact Form 7 form with AI?

Yes, if you bring your own API key. Describe the form in plain English and Bina asks your provider to draft it. It asks a question or two when the request is genuinely ambiguous, shows you the fields it proposes before anything is created, and lets you ask for changes. Every generation reports what it cost in tokens. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini all work, and the feature does nothing at all until an administrator saves a key.

Is this compatible with my theme and with popular page builders like Elementor and Divi?

Yes. Bina forms stay ordinary Contact Form 7 forms, so you place them on a page exactly as you always have: the shortcode, the Contact Form 7 block, or a form widget in a builder like Elementor or Divi. To be clear about which tool does what, you build and edit the form in Bina, and the page builder only places it on the page. Bina’s optional styling is light and only touches the forms it manages.

Does this work with my Contact Form 7 add-ons?

Yes. Tags from CF7 add-ons are imported, kept intact, and written back exactly as they were on push. You can still edit their name, label, required flag and raw options in the builder.

Will this restyle my other Contact Form 7 forms?

No. Bina’s front-end styling only applies to forms Bina manages. Your other CF7 forms keep the look they have. You can also switch the styles off completely with the bina_load_form_styles filter.

What happens to my Contact Form 7 mail settings?

They are kept. Bina round-trips CF7’s mail, mail (2) and messages settings on import and on push. You still edit them in the CF7 admin tabs you already know.

What data does Bina send externally?

By default, nothing. Two optional features can send something, and only once you have switched them on:

  1. Anonymous, non-personal usage data (WordPress, PHP and Contact Form 7 versions, the plugin version, and which features get used), if you opt in. You can opt out again at any time.
  2. The AI form generator, if an administrator saves an API key for an AI provider. Only the description you type is sent, from your own server to that provider.

Your form entries and your visitors’ data are never sent anywhere by either feature.

How does the AI form generator work?

It does nothing until an administrator opens Bina, picks a provider (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini), and saves an API key from their own account. Nothing is sent before that, and deleting the key switches the feature off again.

When you generate a form, your server sends the description you typed straight to the provider you chose, using your key. If you ask for changes, the working form structure goes along so the model can edit it. That is the whole of what is sent: no entries, no visitor data, no site content, and nothing passing through our servers. Your usage is billed by the provider you picked and governed by their terms. See the terms and privacy policies for OpenAI (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/ and https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/), Anthropic (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) and Google (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy).

Your API key is stored encrypted in your own database and is never shown again once saved, beyond the last four characters so you can tell which key it is. If you would rather the feature did not exist at all, define BINA_DISABLE_AI in wp-config.php and it is gone.

Which third-party service powers the optional analytics?

Freemius, Inc. The opt-in usage analytics and the deactivation feedback form both go through them. Data is sent only if you opt in, and only the anonymous, non-personal information described above. It never includes your form entries or your visitors’ data, and nothing is sent if you skip the opt-in or opt out later. See the Freemius Terms of Service (https://freemius.com/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://freemius.com/privacy/).

Where are entries stored, and is it GDPR-friendly?

In your own WordPress database, nowhere else. Bina hooks into WordPress’s privacy tools, so personal data in entries is included in the Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data requests under Tools. You can also switch off entry storage for any form with the bina_store_entry filter.

What happens to my Contact Form 7 entries if I delete the plugin?

Deactivating changes nothing: your entries stay in the database and your forms keep working as normal Contact Form 7 forms. Deleting the plugin is different. WordPress runs Bina’s cleanup, which drops the entries table along with Bina’s own settings and drafts. Export your entries to CSV first if you want to keep them.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: AI form generation. Describe the form you want and your own AI provider drafts it. It runs on your own API key and stays off until an administrator adds one.
  • Appearance now has Normal, Hover and Focus states for fields, Normal and Hover for the submit button, field height, and border width and corner radius per side and per corner.
  • Required fields show a * beside the label, which you can recolor or hide. Existing forms pick this up after the update.
  • Fixed: Minor issues.

1.0.2

  • Added optional, opt-in anonymous usage analytics and a deactivation feedback form (powered by Freemius). No data is sent unless you opt in; form entries never leave your site.
  • Added a friendly, one-time prompt (shown after a week of use) inviting happy users to leave a WordPress.org review. Fully optional and dismissible.

1.0.1

  • Improved import accuracy for theme-styled and placeholder-based forms.
  • Added detection for forms edited directly in Contact Form 7, with a lock and “Edit with Bina” shortcut in the CF7 editor.
  • Minor bug fixes and interface polish.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release: visual drag-and-drop builder for Contact Form 7, one-click import, draft/push workflow with conflict detection and 24-hour rollback, autosave with crash recovery, entry storage with search and CSV export, GDPR export/erase integration, front-end preview, scoped form styling, and full CF7 option round-trip.

short_description: Drag-and-drop Contact Form 7 builder. Import existing forms, save submissions to your database, style forms and add responsive columns without CSS.
